newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts quiet in thin trade, await auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts quiet in thin trade, await auction.

text.p: Indian government securities were largely steady in thin early-afternoon trade Monday as traders turned cautious and kept to the sidelines ahead of a bond auction later in the day.
"At the moment, the market is almost dead," said a dealer. "Everyone is waiting for the auction results."
The central bank auctions 50 billion rupees of four-year bonds later on Monday and dealers said they expect the auction to be fully-subscribed.
Market players forecast a wide range for the yield on the bond, between 10.75 and 11.05 percent.
Four-year paper currently trades around 10.65 percent in the secondary market.
The 12.59 percent 2004 traded at 104.92 and 104.96 rupees against its last traded 104.95 and the 12.14 percent 2000 stock at 104.25 against 104.27.
The 13.50 percent 1998 traded at 103.85 against 103.82 while the 13.85 percent 2006 eased to 111.60 from 111.62.
